title: Problem 1
statement_text: Does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm which, given a near-triangulation $G$ with the outer face bounded by a 4-cycle $C$ and a 4-coloring $\psi$ of $C$, correctly decides whether $\psi$ extends to a 4-coloring of $G$?
context_text: A near-triangulation is a connected plane graph in which all faces except the outer one have length three. By the Four Color Theorem every planar graph is 4-colourable, but many natural follow-up questions are wide open, and even very basic precoloring extension questions such as this one are unresolved. There exist infinitely many near-triangulations whose outer face is bounded by a $4$-cycle $C$ such that not every $4$-colouring of $C$ extends to a $4$-colouring of $G$, and the authors have no good guess at how such near-triangulations could be described. Some information is known: writing $n^\star_G(\psi)$ for the number of extensions of a colouring $\psi$ of $C=v_1v_2v_3v_4$, a standard Kempe chain argument shows that if the colouring $(1,2,1,2)$ extends, then $(1,2,3,2)$ or $(1,2,1,4)$ extends, and block-count reducibility gives linear inequalities that the vector of extension counts must satisfy (a cone in $\mathbb{R}^3$).

title: Conjecture 8
statement_text: Every plane near-cubic graph $\tilde{G}$ with $d(\tilde{G}) = 5$ satisfies $n_{\tilde{G}} \in B'_5$.
context_text: Graphs may have loops and parallel edges. A near-cubic graph $\tilde G=(G,v,\nu)$ is a connected graph $G$ with a vertex $v$ such that every other vertex has degree $3$, together with a numbering $\nu$ of the half-edges at $v$ by $0,\dots,\deg(v)-1$; it is plane if $G$ is plane and these half-edges appear in this clockwise order around $v$, and $d(\tilde G)=\deg(v)$. A $3$-edge-colouring of $\tilde G$ colours the edges with $1,2,3$ so that edges sharing a vertex other than $v$ get distinct colours; a $d$-precolouring is a map $\psi:\{0,\dots,d-1\}\to\{1,2,3\}$ in which each colour is used a number of times of the same parity as $d$, and $n_{\tilde G}(\psi)$ is the number of $3$-edge-colourings whose colours on the half-edges at $v$ are given by $\psi$. Dually, $n_{\tilde G}$ counts the extensions of $4$-colourings of the outer cycle of the near-triangulation $G^\star$ whose outer face corresponds to $v$. Using Kempe chains through $v$ (their endpoints and parities), the authors define for each $d$ a polyhedral coloring count cone $B_d\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{\mathcal{P}_d}$ ($\mathcal{P}_d$ the set of $d$-precolourings) and prove that $n_{\tilde G}\in B_{d(\tilde G)}$ for every plane near-cubic graph. The cone $B_5$ has exactly $12$ rays, spanned by $n_{\tilde R_{5,1}},\dots,n_{\tilde R_{5,12}}$ for explicit near-cubic graphs; the first eleven are plane, while $\tilde R_{5,12}$ is not (glued with the $5$-wheel it gives the Petersen graph), and $B'_5$ is the subcone spanned by the first eleven rays. The statement that no non-zero $n_{\tilde G}$ of a plane $\tilde G$ lies on the ray of $\tilde R_{5,12}$ is equivalent to the Four Color Theorem, so this conjecture strengthens it. Equivalently (as $B'_5$ has a single facet not shared with $B_5$): $3\sum_{i=0}^4 n_{\tilde G}(\psi^{a}_i)\ge\sum_{i=0}^4 n_{\tilde G}(\psi^{b}_i)$, where $\psi^a_i(j)$ and $\psi^b_i(j)$ are given, for $(j-i)\bmod5=0,1,2,3,4$, by $1,1,2,3,1$ and $1,2,1,1,3$ respectively. The authors verify it for all plane near-cubic graphs with fewer than $30$ vertices.

title: Conjecture 9
statement_text: Every plane near-cubic graph $\tilde{G}$ with $d(\tilde{G}) = 5$ satisfies $$\sum_{i=0}^{4} n_{\tilde{G}}(\psi^{5,a}_i) \geq \sum_{i=0}^{4} n_{\tilde{G}}(\psi^{5,b}_i).$$
context_text: The cone $B'_5$ has exactly one facet that is not also a facet of $B_5$, and this inequality captures precisely that facet, giving an equivalent reformulation of Conjecture 8. Here $\psi^{5,a}_i$ and $\psi^{5,b}_i$ are specific 5-precolorings (for $i \in \{0,\ldots,4\}$) defined by rotating two base precolorings of the 5-half-edges around $v$.
